claims_scope: The machine re-checks the DECLARED universal claims of the K1344 single-owner note: the 17 floor-18 cell closed forms F23f18..A1123f18 (F23f18 = the FOURTEENTH tail form, odd-z HOLE+TAIL: single point s=22=z-1 DOWN 1v2, conforming hole s=23=z, persistent tail UP 2v0 for s>=24; A23f18 = the A-RANK BREAK REBIRTH at s=18=z-5, odd-z birth 4/4; A1123f18 = the NINTH consecutive in-band base child), the strip theorem T-Z23 (min>=18; base m=18 trivial absorption through the fully collapsing A1123f18), corollaries 1-2 (z*(18)=34 closes the slice; min=18 row z in {0..23}, residual band z in {24..33}, frontier 34). Battery points are finite engine cross-checks; the universal claims are proven on paper in the declaration note section 2 from the published lemmas (K0832, K1138, K1264, K1312, K1268, K1334) and the published z=22 lines (K1339), the latter independently re-anchored here (D3) rather than taken on faith. The drafting machine was named verify_tz23.py and renamed to verify_k1344.py after the declaration push (66ac2775); the rename touches only the machine label and docstring bytes and the battery structure is unchanged (disclosed in the note section 4/section 6).
protocol: publish-then-execute: official runs executed from the PUBLISHED bytes (fetch-back sha256-verified against the local machine; git blob sha1 019b3970c459ea899e48060471cd4ac64459f366) after machine publication; runs r1/r2 in the publishing workdir (default / PYTHONHASHSEED=random), runs r3/r4 env -i isolated dirs via /usr/local/bin/python3. Tamper battery also re-executed from the published bytes (8/8 FAIL-CLOSED, byte-identical to the renamed-bytes predry tamper outputs). Predry before publication on the renamed bytes: 8 runs byte-identical (default x2, PYTHONHASHSEED=random/1/0 same-cwd, env -i isolated x3), stdout 671 bytes. Drafting bytes (verify_tz23.py, sha256 2b22acec210d9517d43e1a293953666f9bde82c85280c391417cce8522bfe7ed): predry 8 runs byte-identical (stdout 670 bytes), tamper 8/8 fail-closed. Honest run record: the first attempt of r3/r4 copied the published bytes under the wrong filename (fb1344.py) and produced an immediate 'file not found' rc 2 with an EMPTY output; the slip was caught by the empty-file check and redone correctly within the same session before any output was frozen; the published run3.out/run4.out are the corrected runs.
